correctness_confidence.basis: I re-derived the necessity pairing (7)-(9) (means of F,G, skew-adjointness, minimisation at c=a^{1/3}), the factorisation/angular identity of Lemma 2, the Poisson-smoothing and quantile error bound of Prop. 4 (constants 4*pi*sigma/(N tau^2) and 256*pi*b^2/delta^3 check out), the local-analytic leading-term argument (17) and the k-harmonic scaling of Cor. 6. I also numerically checked Lemma 3 for c=0.3,1,2.5 (h_c(0)=1, Re h_c>=0 and w_c>=0 on the circle to ~1e-9). No error found; I did not check every boundary-exceptional-point detail rigorously.

rigor.basis: Proofs are mostly complete but terse: Lemma 3 exceptional-point behaviour and the claim that f_c has no zero in the disc are asserted rather than shown; Prop. 5 compactness step (Fourier-degree drop) is sketched; Cor. 6 sufficiency for general k and negative omega is a brief reduction. Quantile selection is not certified.

novelty.basis: Exact threshold |b|^{2/3}<1+a^{2/3} for the Liu-Fitzsimmons family (arXiv:2607.16171, which I confirmed exists and only gives a sufficient nonexistence region |b|>=2(a+1) per this paper) appears to be new relative to what I found; but tools (Fejer-Riesz, Hilbert transform, positive harmonic functions, binary-form SOS) are classical and unbounded degree is known (Ahmadi-Parrilo). I did not fully read the Liu-Fitzsimmons text, so overlap beyond their abstract is unchecked.

significance.basis: Complete sharp classification for one explicit two-parameter family and its single-harmonic generalisation; useful as a clean model of the polynomial-converse failure, but it does not yield a general theorem or the minimum-degree rate, and certificate classification does not alter stability.

reproducibility.basis: Argument is analytic and explicit with closed-form constants; the numerical diagnostics are described honestly as non-certified. I reproduced the key boundary identities numerically in floating point; I did not run the author's code.

summary: The manuscript proves that for the Liu-Fitzsimmons cubic family (a>0, b real) positive homogeneous polynomial weak certificates, strict ones (as products of positive quadratic forms), and local real-analytic certificates all exist exactly when |b|^{2/3}<1+a^{2/3}. Necessity uses a Hilbert-transform pairing with an explicit analytic test function; sufficiency uses an explicit limiting harmonic pair, Poisson smoothing and quantile discretisation giving an explicit degree bound O(delta^-3). Extensions to single even harmonics with angular speed and an SOS corollary are given. In my checks the main claims are correct and honestly scoped (no minimum-degree rate, no priority claim, AI assistance and non-independence of review disclosed). The result is a neat but narrow sharpening of a recent counterexample.
strengths: Sharp, explicit and checkable threshold with strict exclusion of equality
Clean unification of polynomial, SOS and local analytic certificates
Explicit degree bound with verified constants
Honest limitations and disclosure of review status
weaknesses: Narrow scope: one parametric family plus single-harmonic variants
Some steps (Lemma 3 exceptional points, Prop. 5 compactness, Cor. 6 reductions) are terse
No matching degree rates; quantile construction not certified
Novelty depends on a very recent preprint; no formal verification
potential_errors: Lemma 3: boundary regularity at the simple zero z=eta^3... and pole of M_c is asserted briefly; I only checked numerically.
Cor. 6: claim that rotation by an angle flips b for general k and the omega<0 reduction are stated without detail (appear correct).
Cor. 7 rational-coefficient remark is only sketched.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact threshold |b|^{2/3}<1+a^{2/3} via the extremal harmonic problem with boundary limiting pair and its k-harmonic form |b|^{2/3}<a^{2/3}+|omega|^{2/3}
